purpose: Separate GPU kernel execution, host launch gaps and CPU affinity in the current small independent-model workload.

protocol.timing_includes: observe, action, world step, next observe, L3 learning, inheritance check
protocol.timing_excludes: initial compile, warmup, profiler, numerical check, observer/log/checkpoint I/O
protocol.governor: powersave; CPU/GPU clocks were not forced
limitations: One process per GPU/affinity/precision case plus an extra FP32 repetition on CPU16-19; fixed order, not randomized.
Profiler durations come from separate 12-tick traces and must not be subtracted from unprofiled wall times.
Kernel-free gaps in the trace include host work, launch/scheduling latency, dependency or synchronization waits, and profiler overhead; they do not isolate a single cause.
ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0 probe changes an environment variable, but does not independently prove which backend ran.
Affinity changes did not isolate a causal CPU-core effect: repeating the same CPU16-19 mask changed R9700 FP32 from 5.91 to 6.55 ms/tick.
Pinning the main thread to CPU16 leaves the autograd worker on CPU16-19; profiler perturbation was larger in this probe.
The ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0 probe showed no improvement versus the adjacent default repeat; neither backend choice nor backend-specific root cause is proved.

supported: R9700 has shorter GPU kernel execution time than V620 for the measured FP32 compiled workload.
Faster GPU kernel execution does not translate proportionally into lower unprofiled wall time for this workload.
Many small kernels, per-agent matrix-vector products, and a per-tick synchronization in birth detection leave host/launch/dependency latency on the critical path.
The previous cross-GPU wall-time ranking included different CPU affinity masks and concurrent benchmark processes; it is not a clean comparison of raw GPU arithmetic.
not_established: The exact contribution of CPU affinity versus background activity, clock policy, scheduling, and runtime/library internals.
A specific hipBLASLt, rocBLAS, or driver bug causing the timing gap.
Universal GPU ranking, sustained GPU utilization, or a hardware-speedup ratio from separately profiled kernel times.
